No hands-on LIDAR/Radar sensor integration at vehicle scale

semantic_recommendation: Do not apply. The 3+ year production requirement is a hard gate at new grad stage. Revisit in 2-3 years of industry experience. Strong fit signals (ROS, embedded, CAD) suggest this role is a natural next step post-PhD or post-production-years.

strengths: Proven end-to-end system integration (COFFIN): three-layer distributed pipeline, 11 resolved integration failures, 100% reliability.
Real-time embedded expertise (FreeRTOS, STM32 bare-metal, interrupt-driven UART)—directly applicable to vehicle control loops.
Component-level electrical thinking (Jetson, ToF sensors, I2C mux, servo control, power sequencing).
Design rigor and documentation (specs, latency profiling, failure analysis).
ROS/robotics fundamentals (kinematics, collision avoidance, visual servoing).
real_gaps: Zero hands-on LIDAR/Radar integration. JD lists these as core; you have cameras only (missing 70% of perception stack).

No production vehicle electrical integration. All work is lab-scale robotics. Vehicle electrical includes power distribution, EMI/RFI shielding, safety redundancy, long-cycle reliability—different domain.
CAN Bus and Ethernet not evidenced. You have UART/I2C/SPI; vehicles use CAN for distributed real-time control and Ethernet for high-bandwidth sensor data. Hard gap, not adjacent.
No customer interaction/field deployment experience. JD emphasizes travel to customer sites for installation/troubleshooting.
Supply chain and vendor management not evidenced. JD explicitly requires this; your profile shows internal fabrication only.
overstated_by_keywords: 'Autonomous systems' match: CARLA sim and ROS are strong, but production vehicle autonomy involves legal liability and safety certification.
'System integration' match: Lab components (Jetson+Arduino) vs vehicle electrical subsystems (powertrain, CAN gateway). Scale matters.
understated_by_keywords: STM32 bare-metal firmware with deterministic timing is exactly the low-level control layer vehicle engineers need—undersold by keywords.
FreeRTOS + interrupt-driven design aligns with vehicle control loop requirements more than keyword score suggests.
screening_gaps: Zero production vehicle electrical integration (JD requires 3+ years; you have 0 FT years, all research/capstone).
LIDAR/Radar perception missing (core to autonomy; cameras alone are 25% of the sensor suite JD requires).
CAN Bus/Ethernet not evidenced (vehicle-specific networking standard; UART/I2C/SPI don't substitute).
llm_analysis.reasoning: Keyword score (68%) is solid; semantic depth shows production scope mismatch. All work is lab/research; role demands shipping production vehicles. LIDAR/Radar are core, learnable but require 12–18 months. CAN/Ethernet are vehicle-specific infrastructure. 3-year gate is structural. Partial Fit, not Strong Fit.
